title: Dedicated Capacity Autoscaling Bounds — Migration Plan (Existing Deployments)
content:
Doc purpose
- Provide a step-by-step plan to roll out autoscaling bounds (min/max + predictive toggle) to existing Dedicated deployments without changing behavior until explicitly enabled.
- Define defaulting semantics, opt-in flow, verification/monitoring, and safe rollback.

Scope
- Existing Dedicated deployments (already in production) across supported regions.
- Control plane schema + storage changes, autoscaler enforcement, feature flags, observability, and audit logging.
- Predictive mode is treated as a separate opt-in that depends on bounds plumbing (but can be rolled out after bounds-only GA).

Non-goals
- Contract renegotiation workflows.
- Auto-procurement based on predictions.
- Cross-region capacity placement optimization.

Definitions / Key semantics
- “Legacy behavior” = current autoscaler logic using platform defaults + reactive signals (saturation/queue depth) and any existing operator overrides.
- “Bounds enabled” = autoscaler clamps desired replicas to [min_replicas, max_replicas] after it computes desired from signals.
- “Unset bounds fields” are not interpreted as 0 or infinity. They are treated as “no customer constraint” (i.e., do not change legacy behavior).

Critical invariants (must hold throughout migration)
1) Backward compatibility: existing deployments must not change scaling behavior unless bounds_enabled is explicitly true.
2) Safety: when enabled, never exceed max_replicas, never scale below min_replicas.
3) Determinism/auditability: record requested_desired, bounded_desired, and decision_reason for every scaling tick (bounded or not).
4) Fail-safe: if policy fetch fails or policy is invalid, autoscaler falls back to legacy behavior unless bounds_enabled is true and the last-known-good policy is available in cache (see failure modes).

Data model and defaulting behavior
Control plane fields (conceptual)
- bounds_enabled: boolean (default false)
- min_replicas: integer or null
- max_replicas: integer or null
- scale_up_cooldown_seconds: integer (default legacy)
- scale_down_cooldown_seconds: integer (default legacy)
- predictive_mode: enum {off, on} (default off)
- predictive_lead_time_seconds: integer (optional, gated)

Defaulting rules for existing deployments
- bounds_enabled defaults to false for all existing deployments.
- min_replicas and max_replicas default to null/unset.
- When bounds_enabled=false:
  - autoscaler ignores min/max fields entirely.
  - behavior should match pre-migration behavior (including any platform defaults).
- When bounds_enabled=true:
  - if min_replicas is null => treat as 0 for clamping purposes OR reject? Decision: reject enablement if min_replicas or max_replicas are null.
  - if max_replicas is null => reject enablement.
  - Rationale: we want explicit customer intent and avoid ambiguous behavior. Console/API should require both min and max before enabling.

Implementation note: We still store nullable min/max to support staged config entry (set values now, enable later), but enforce that enabling requires both.

Feature flags / gating
- Account-level: dedicated_bounds_enabled_account (allows writing bounds config + autoscaler reading it)
- Deployment-level: dedicated_bounds_enabled_deployment (actual enforcement switch)
- Predictive mode flag (separate): dedicated_predictive_autoscaling

Operationally:
- For pilots: enable account-level first (lets CS/eng set config), then enable deployment-level once values are validated and dashboards are ready.
- For GA: account-level defaults on for Dedicated accounts, but deployment-level remains customer-configured.

Migration plan overview (phased)
Phase 0 — Pre-migration readiness (1–2 weeks)
Owner(s): Michael Nguyen (migrations), Ethan Park (control plane), Vanessa Ortiz (autoscaler), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Allison Grant (obs)
1) Confirm final semantics in ADR (bounds precedence, safety invariants, failure modes).
2) Confirm DB schema + rollout strategy (additive, nullable fields).
3) Confirm validation rules:
   - min_replicas >= 0
   - max_replicas >= 1
   - min_replicas <= max_replicas
   - max_replicas must be <= contractual ceiling if a contract ceiling exists (control plane validation hook).
   - cooldowns in allowed ranges.
4) Confirm audit event shape and retention requirements (enterprise accounts).
5) Prepare dashboards and alert rules (at least: bound_hit counters, desired vs bounded, queue depth, unmet_min state).
6) Prepare “disable switch” for rapid rollback:
   - a global kill switch to force bounds_enabled=false in autoscaler evaluation (emergency only), scoped per region.

Exit criteria Phase 0
- Schema and validation are reviewed.
- Autoscaler changes are behind flags.
- Observability and runbook drafts exist.

Phase 1 — Ship additive schema + read path (no behavior changes)
1) Deploy control plane schema changes:
   - Add new fields to deployment config storage.
   - Ensure API/serialization includes new fields but defaults to bounds_enabled=false.
2) Deploy autoscaler code that can parse policy but does not enforce unless deployment flag is on.
3) Start emitting metrics/logs in “shadow mode”:
   - requested_desired (legacy)
   - bounded_desired (computed as if bounds were enabled ONLY when bounds_enabled=true; otherwise equal to requested_desired)
   - bound_hit_{min|max} counters (should be 0 for all existing deployments)
4) Add internal admin CLI commands:
   - dump-effective-policy --deployment_id
   - show-last-decisions --deployment_id --lookback

Verification checklist Phase 1
- Sampling: compare scale decisions before/after deploy for a subset of deployments (should match).
- Metrics cardinality: confirm labels are bounded (deployment_id optional; prefer hashed or sampled).

Rollback Phase 1
- Safe to rollback binaries: new fields are additive and ignored by legacy binaries.
- Do not remove columns/fields.

Phase 2 — Backfill / migration defaults for existing deployments
Goal: ensure all existing deployments have explicit bounds_enabled=false recorded to avoid future ambiguity.
1) Backfill job (idempotent):
   - For each Dedicated deployment missing scaling_policy object, create scaling_policy with bounds_enabled=false, predictive_mode=off.
   - Leave min_replicas/max_replicas null.
   - Write audit event: scaling_policy_backfilled (actor=system).
2) Rate-limit backfill writes to avoid control plane load spikes.
3) Post-backfill validation:
   - % deployments with scaling_policy present should reach ~100%.
   - No change in scaling behavior expected.

Rollback Phase 2
- Backfill is write-only but should not affect behavior.
- If backfill causes control plane load issues: stop job; no further action required.

Phase 3 — Pilot enablement (bounds-only)
Goal: enable hard min/max enforcement for a small set of existing deployments.
Prereqs
- SRE runbook available.
- Alerts configured (max-bound saturation + queue buildup; unmet-min due to region shortage).
- Account flagged in internal system and documented in pilot tracker.

Step-by-step pilot flow (per account)
1) Enable account-level feature flag: dedicated_bounds_enabled_account=true.
   - Verify customer is aware; capture approvals (CS + SRE) if required.
2) Set bounds values while bounds_enabled remains false:
   - min_replicas = customer baseline
   - max_replicas = customer spend cap
   - (optional) cooldown tweaks if needed
   - Validate via control plane (min<=max, contractual ceiling).
3) Dry-run validation (internal):
   - Use admin CLI to confirm effective policy.
   - Use dashboard to ensure requested_desired and bounded_desired are sane under current load.
4) Enable enforcement:
   - Set deployment-level flag dedicated_bounds_enabled_deployment=true.
   - Set bounds_enabled=true in policy.
5) Monitor for 48–72 hours:
   - bound_hit_max rate (if high + sustained queue depth, customer max too low or workload changed)
   - queue depth / p95 latency during ramps
   - scale event churn / oscillation (should not increase)

Pilot rollback (per deployment)
- Preferred rollback (fast):
  1) Flip deployment-level flag dedicated_bounds_enabled_deployment=false.
  2) bounds_enabled can remain true in config but will be ignored while flag is off.
- Secondary rollback (config):
  1) Set bounds_enabled=false.
  2) Keep min/max values for later reuse.
- Emergency rollback (region kill switch):
  - Used only if there is systemic impact (autoscaler bug). Forces bounds enforcement off for all deployments in region.

Notes
- If customer is at max and queue depth rises, the system is behaving correctly (respecting spend cap). CS should treat as capacity/cost tradeoff conversation, not necessarily an incident.

Phase 4 — Expand pilot + introduce predictive mode (optional)
Predictive mode increases risk (bad forecasts can cause oscillation/overshoot). Roll out only after bounds-only behavior is stable.
1) Keep bounds enabled.
2) Enable dedicated_predictive_autoscaling at account level.
3) Turn predictive_mode=on for a single deployment first.
4) Staleness rules:
   - if forecast is stale/unavailable => fall back to reactive desired (still clamped).
5) Monitor prediction error + impact on p95 latency.

Rollback predictive mode
- Set predictive_mode=off OR disable dedicated_predictive_autoscaling flag.
- Bounds remain active.

Phase 5 — GA migration posture (what “done” looks like)
- Bounds capability is available to all Dedicated customers.
- Existing customers remain unchanged until they enable bounds.
- New Dedicated deployments (post-GA) may have bounds recommended in Console, but should not auto-enable without explicit customer action (unless Product decides otherwise in a separate launch).

Customer-facing defaulting behavior (Console/API)
- Console should allow setting min/max while enforcement is disabled (draft state).
- Console should show:
  - current replicas
  - recommended min/max range (soft guidance)
  - projected cost impact at min/max
  - explicit warning: “Enabling bounds enforces a hard max; requests may queue if demand exceeds max.”
- Enable toggle should be blocked until both min and max are provided.

Risk analysis + mitigations
1) Risk: accidental behavior change due to default interpretation of null
- Mitigation: bounds_enabled=false by default; enforcement requires both values + explicit enable.

2) Risk: control plane partial rollout leads to mixed versions
- Mitigation: additive fields; autoscaler should treat missing policy as legacy.

3) Risk: region capacity shortage prevents meeting min
- Expected behavior: system enters “unmet_min” degraded state; keeps retrying with backoff; alerts SRE + surfaces to customer.
- Mitigation: alerting + clear customer comms template.

4) Risk: config churn (customer toggles frequently)
- Mitigation: rate limit policy updates; emit warnings/audit events.

5) Risk: max-bound saturation causes customer-visible latency spikes
- Mitigation: proactive dashboard + CS playbook; routing can degrade gracefully (fallback model/region if policy allows) without violating bounds.

Validation / Observability requirements (minimum)
Metrics
- dedicated.autoscaler.desired_replicas (requested)
- dedicated.autoscaler.bounded_desired_replicas
- dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total{bound=min|max}
- dedicated.autoscaler.unmet_min (gauge)
- dedicated.queue.depth
- dedicated.saturation.gpu_utilization
Logs / audit events
- scaling_policy_updated (actor, fields changed)
- autoscaler_decision (requested_desired, bounded_desired, reasons, signals)
- scaling_policy_backfilled (system)

Rollout checklist (per region)
- [ ] Control plane schema deployed
- [ ] Autoscaler binary deployed with flags off
- [ ] Dashboards available
- [ ] Alerts installed and tested (synthetic trigger if available)
- [ ] Runbook published + on-call trained
- [ ] Kill switch validated

Appendix A — Suggested operational runbooks (links)
- Dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting runbook (SRE)
- Bounds observability dashboard spec (Observability)
- Known issues: predictive autoscaling (if predictive enabled)

Appendix B — Example migration timeline (illustrative)
Week 1: Phase 1 ship (schema + autoscaler shadow)
Week 2: Phase 2 backfill
Week 3: Phase 3 pilot enablement (2–3 accounts)
Week 4–5: expand pilot + harden alerts/runbooks
Week 6: GA bounds-only; predictive remains gated

Open questions (as of last edit)
- Do we allow bounds_enabled=true with only one of min/max set by interpreting null as “no clamp”? (current recommendation: NO; require both.)
- Should we automatically populate recommended min/max for existing deployments based on recent peaks? (nice-to-have; keep out of migration to minimize risk.)
- What is the exact contractual ceiling source-of-truth (CRM vs control plane contract record) and what is the validation fallback if contract data is missing?
